desc: The tethered smoke harness reports FAILURE on a SUCCESSFUL boot, which is a misattribution hazard proven live. In the passing ticket-147 run (2026-07-26 13:58) scripts/t6040-boot-raw-object.sh printed 'chainload failed; last output:' and exited non-zero even though the object booted perfectly (full health report, shell prompt, all criteria met). Root cause: chainload.py ends with iface.nop(), which necessarily times out (UartTimeout: Expected 1 bytes, got 0) once Linux takes over the UART and the m1n1 proxy is gone — i.e. proxy loss after a successful handoff is the EXPECTED outcome of a one-object smoke, not an error. Today three people-hours went into distinguishing real wrong-object failures from this cosmetic one; a future reader will mistake a pass for a fail or vice versa. FIX: have the wrapper treat post-handoff proxy loss as success when the boot markers are present (e.g. 'health report end' / a shell prompt in the log), and reserve non-zero exit for real failures (SHA mismatch, no handoff, panic, no markers). Report a clear verdict line instead of leaking a Python traceback. Offline scriptable; verify against the 2026-07-26 logs (one passing, two wrong-object) with no rig time. Evidence: done/2026-07-26-t6040-dietcap-kernel-smoke-result.md.
